summary.text: A 68-year-old Asian woman presented with a 1-year history of heartburn and weight loss, weighing 43 kg with a BMI of 16.8 kg/m^(2). Her history was unremarkable. CT showed a 15 cm pelvic cystic mass with peritoneal effusion, CA-125 was 309.2 U/mL and hemoglobin 95 g/L, and ovarian malignancy was suspected.

Laparoscopic exploration was converted to open laparotomy because of severe adhesions, and the left ovary and fallopian tube were resected. Frozen section suggested a benign cystic adenoma. She was fasted for 1 week after surgery and given parenteral nutrition, and had irregular fever that improved with treatment. Pathology showed a benign mucinous cystic adenoma and necrotic granulomatous tissue considered tuberculosis, with positive tuberculin skin and interferon-gamma release assays.

She was discharged on postoperative day 14 and developed a sudden fever of 39 ℃ that evening. CT suggested and intestinal imaging showed colonic perforation at the descending sigmoid junction, and the incision exuded loose stool. An enterocutaneous fistula was confirmed. Management included octreotide, drainage, nutritional support and intravenous then oral antituberculosis therapy.

She continued antituberculosis treatment at home with daily drainage care. After 1.5 years the drainage was withdrawn, the incision healed and the fistula healed completely. Her weight increased to 55 kg, her appetite improved and bowel and urinary function recovered; the authors describe a full recovery.

article_limitations: Table 1 day counts relative to admission and the text's postoperative day counts are not reconciled; see the ambiguities.
Tuberculosis was not microbiologically confirmed (AFB smear, culture and molecular testing were not performed).
The suspected ovarian malignancy is not stated as excluded; the final pathology is a benign adenoma.
Literature discussion (cited studies on CA-125, HE4, interferon-gamma release assay, Xpert, ADA, imaging and biopsy) is not patient data and is not recorded.
Figure captions are author statements; pixel descriptions are in visual.json.
